grade.first_issue: The decisive relation c x_O-bx'_O=(c^2-b^2)/4 is merely asserted to follow from “symmetry.” It is exactly equivalent to the desired conclusion, while the cross-angle constraints ∠LBK=α₂ and ∠LCK=α₃ are never used to derive it. This is an unsupported central compatibility claim under Rule E.
grade.summary: The submission makes meaningful coordinate progress and correctly reduces OM=ON to a linear condition on O, but it provides no proof of that condition. Although the missing equality is explicit and true, Rule B does not make a score of 4 eligible because the preceding reduction is not correct and complete: the L-coordinate construction has the wrong orientation, angle branches and possible right-angle cases are untreated, and two essential angle constraints remain unused.
strengths: The coordinates of A, B, C, M, and N are set up correctly.
For generic non-right angles, the calculation of K from the conditions at B and M is correct.
The perpendicular-bisector formulation for a circumcentre is appropriate.
The algebraic reduction of OM=ON to c x_O-bx'_O=(c^2-b^2)/4 is correct.

errors.description: The final linear relation for O is asserted without calculation or geometric argument. Calling it a consequence of symmetry is insufficient and essentially assumes the conclusion; proving this relation is the central difficulty of the problem.

In the stated AC-coordinate system, B has negative y'-coordinate, hence an interior point L of triangle BNC must lie on that side of AC. The correct oriented lines have signs opposite to those written. Thus the submitted formulas construct the reflection of L across AC, and the ensuing AL perpendicular-bisector equation is not for the actual L.
The equalities ∠LBK=∠LNC and ∠LCK=∠BMK supply essential compatibility between the separately constructed K and L, but their cross-angle sides are never translated into equations or otherwise used.

The tangent and cotangent calculations do not treat, or prove impossible, cases in which one of the relevant angles is 90°, and the required angle-branch choices are not justified from the interior hypotheses.
